name: Mirror Brusquembille
summary: Two-player, 16-trick card game. Each player draws from an identical private 16-card pile, and the follower must follow suit only in the last three tricks.

player.meaning: Card points won in tricks, plus the 1-point bonus if this player won trick 16.
Cards in this player's hand, 3 at most. Each card is a two-letter code: rank A/T/K/7, then suit S/H/D/C (e.g. 'TH').
Number of cards left in this player's own pile.

game.meaning: Seat 1's private pile. Its order and contents are hidden from both players.
Seat 2's private pile, hidden from both players.
Trump suit letter (S, H, D or C), drawn at random during setup.
Seat (1 or 2) that leads the current trick.
Number of the current trick, 1 to 16. It becomes 17 when the game ends.
Card the leader played face up in the current trick.
Card the follower played face up in the current trick.
Every card played face up so far, in order, with the seat that played it.
Seat that won the trick just played.

setup: Each seat's pile (pile_1, pile_2) holds the 16 cards: one Ace, Ten, King and Seven of each of the four suits. Both players are told this composition.
Each seat draws 3 cards at random from its own pile into its hand. Each pile then has 13 cards, and pile_count is set to 13 for both seats.
One suit is drawn at random as trump and announced.
The first leader is chosen at random (seat 1 or 2) and announced.
Both scores are set to 0 and trick is set to 1.

round.effect: Each player sees their own hand plus the public trump, leader, trick, both scores, both pile_count values and played_cards. Neither sees pile_1 or pile_2.
led_card = the chosen card. Remove it from the leader's hand and append it to played_cards. Announce it to both players.

round.who: the seat not equal to leader
round.answer: one card from their hand. If trick >= 14 and they hold a card of led_card's suit, only cards of that suit
round.effect: follow_card = the chosen card. Remove it from the follower's hand and append it to played_cards. Announce it to both players.

Set trick_winner. If exactly one of led_card and follow_card is of the trump suit, its player wins. Otherwise, if both cards share a suit, the follower wins only when follow_card's point value is strictly greater than led_card's (Ace 11 > Ten 10 > King 4 > Seven 0), and the leader wins otherwise, including identical cards. Otherwise (different suits, neither trump) the leader wins. Announce the winner.
Add points(led_card) + points(follow_card) to the winner's score, plus 1 if trick == 16. Points are A=11, T=10, K=4, 7=0. Announce both scores.

Only when trick <= 13: the winner moves one random card from their own pile (pile_1 or pile_2) into their hand and loses 1 pile_count. Then the loser does the same from their own pile. Both hands are back to 3 cards.
End the game if trick > 16. Otherwise play the next trick.

ending.decided_by: After 16 tricks, the player with the higher score wins. The 201 points cannot split evenly, so there is no draw.

rules.text: At setup, each seat's pile holds exactly one A, T, K and 7 of each of the 4 suits: 16 cards worth 100 points.
At setup, each seat draws 3 cards from its own pile into its hand, leaving pile_count = 13 for each seat.
At setup, the trump suit is one of S, H, D, C chosen at random and made public. The first leader is seat 1 or seat 2 at random.
When the game starts, both scores are 0 and trick is 1.
When the leader plays, they may choose any card in their hand, and that card leaves their hand and is added to played_cards.
When trick is 1 to 13, the follower may play any card in their hand.
When trick is 14, 15 or 16 and the follower holds a card of the led suit, the follower must play a card of the led suit.
When trick is 14, 15 or 16 and the follower holds no card of the led suit, the follower may play any card.
When exactly one of the two played cards is a trump, the player of the trump wins the trick (e.g. trump H: 7H beats AS).
When both cards are of the same suit, the higher rank wins, with A > T > K > 7 (e.g. TS beats KS).
When both cards are identical in suit and rank, the leader wins the trick.
When the cards are of different suits and neither is a trump, the leader wins the trick (e.g. trump C, leader 7S, follower AH: the leader wins).
When a player wins a trick, their score increases by the points of both cards, with A=11, T=10, K=4, 7=0 (e.g. AS and TS give +21).
When trick 16 is won, the winner gets 1 bonus point on top of the card points.
When a trick is won, the winner leads the next trick.
When trick is 1 to 13, after the trick the winner and then the loser each draw 1 card from their own pile, each pile_count drops by 1, and both hands return to 3 cards.
When trick is 14, 15 or 16, no cards are drawn, and pile_count is 0 for both seats.
When trick 16 is complete, the game ends and the two scores total 201.
When the game ends, the seat with the higher score wins. A draw is impossible.
Neither player ever sees the cards in pile_1 or pile_2, and each player sees only their own hand.

offers.question: Leader plays a card
offers.options: every card currently in that seat's hand (3 cards in tricks 1 to 14, then 2, then 1)

offers.question: Follower plays a card
offers.who: the seat not equal to leader
offers.options: tricks 1 to 13: every card in hand. Tricks 14 to 16: only the cards in hand of led_card's suit if there is at least one, otherwise every card in hand

choices.why: The designer set 2. The game is a two-player duel of mirrored piles, and every rule (leader/follower, the 201-point total that rules out ties) assumes two seats.
The source has no communication, and in a zero-sum two-player duel talk adds nothing to reason about.

choices.what: Card codes as rank letter plus suit letter (A/T/K/7 with S/H/D/C)
choices.why: A compact text form for list membership and suit/rank tests.
The point values 11 > 10 > 4 > 0 are strictly ordered like the ranks, so comparing points is the same as comparing ranks.

choices.what: The follower is asked after the leader, with ask
choices.why: The rules are sequential: the follower sees the led card before choosing.

A thoughtful player tracks the cards played to infer which cards the opponent still has between hand and pile, saves trumps and high cards for valuable tricks, and plans for the forced-follow endgame of tricks 14 to 16.

simplifications.what: Drawing the 'top card' of a shuffled pile is a random draw from the pile list
simplifications.why: The order is hidden from everyone and fixed by a random shuffle, so a seeded random draw is equivalent.

simplifications.what: Each pile is a hidden table attribute (pile_1, pile_2) rather than a player attribute
simplifications.why: The rules hide a pile even from its owner, and a player attribute cannot be hidden from its owner. Each pile is still drawn only by its own seat, and its public size is kept in that player's pile_count.

simplifications.what: Card points and the trick winner are worked out by conditional arithmetic over the card codes
simplifications.why: The engine has no lookup table, so the 4 rank values and the suit/trump tests are written as if-chains in the update steps.
